**Reasoning:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 50 years. The North China Plain tells you what to grow — winter wheat followed by summer maize. That rotation has fed my family and paid my bills. I'm not going to change it now.

At 70, my back can't take what it used to. I'll hire a local mechanized contractor for the deep rotary tillage before wheat planting and for the combine harvests. My son thinks I should quit, but my mind is still sharp and I know this soil better than any young agronomist.

Water is what keeps me up at night. The water table under Quzhou has been dropping my whole adult life — I've watched it go from 5 meters to over 30 meters since I was young. I used to irrigate wheat 4-5 times. These past years I've cut to 3 careful irrigations and watched my neighbors carefully. Yields held. I'll keep it at 3.

For wheat, I'll use the Jimai 22 variety from the county seed station — it's proven here, good gluten, decent lodging resistance. For maize I'll buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed from the certified dealer in town. I've used it three years running. No point gambling with untested seed at my age.

I apply fertilizer based on what the county extension bulletin says for our soil type — about 18 kg pure nitrogen per mu for wheat, split between base and jointing topdress. I've seen neighbors burn their crops applying too much urea in one go. I won't make that mistake.

I have 10 mu total. I'll farm all of it in the wheat-maize rotation. No vegetables — the market garden plot is more work than it's worth without my wife to help with it.
